note: Seed corpus for the TrustNode prototype: OAuth / PKCE documentation. Trust signals are analyst-seeded (earned) and sample community votes. Real deployments replace seeds with measured track records.

stances.quote: PKCE (RFC 7636) is REQUIRED for public clients using the authorization code flow.

stances.note: Native apps are one example of public clients, not the scope.
stances.quote: The specification defines PKCE for public clients generally — it is not limited to mobile apps.

sources.title: RFC 7636 — Proof Key for Code Exchange by OAuth Public Clients

trust.earned_rationale: Normative IETF standard; primary source for PKCE.

stances.note: Extends the requirement beyond public clients to all authorization code flows.
stances.quote: Clients MUST use PKCE with the authorization code grant — for public and confidential clients alike.

stances.note: The implicit grant is omitted from current best practice due to token exposure in the redirect.
stances.quote: The implicit grant is deprecated: it exposes access tokens in the redirect URI and must not be used.

stances.note: Current best practice explicitly generalizes PKCE past mobile.
stances.quote: PKCE is required for every authorization code flow, including web and single-page applications — not only mobile.

trust.earned_rationale: Current IETF best practice; supersedes older guidance where they conflict.

stances.note: Vendor docs describe PKCE as the standard for apps that cannot keep a secret.
stances.quote: Applications that cannot securely store a client secret — SPAs and native apps — should use the Authorization Code Flow with PKCE.

stances.note: Qualifies the blanket claim: confidential web apps have an alternative.
stances.quote: Regular web applications with a secure backend can use a client secret instead of PKCE.

sources.title: Auth0 Docs — Authorization Code Flow with PKCE

trust.earned_rationale: Vendor documentation; accurate but scoped to Auth0's implementation.

stances.note: General vendor guidance aligned with the standards.
stances.quote: Okta recommends PKCE for all applications using the authorization code flow where the client cannot be fully trusted.

trust.earned_rationale: Vendor documentation from a major identity provider; consistent with RFCs.

stances.note: Outdated framing: true in 2019 practice, superseded by current best practice.
stances.quote: PKCE was designed for mobile apps, so if you're building for iOS or Android, you need it — web apps can skip it.

sources.title: "Do You Need PKCE?" — independent blog post (2019)

trust.earned_rationale: Dated opinion piece; its core claim was true of 2019 practice but is contradicted by current best practice.

stances.note: Community answer reflecting pre-BCP practice; the accepted guidance has since moved on.
stances.quote: For SPAs the implicit flow was the standard approach for years — many tutorials still show it.

sources.title: Stack Overflow answer — "OAuth flow for SPAs" (2021)

trust.earned_rationale: Community Q&A: useful signal of what practitioners believed, not authoritative guidance.
